the cytology of brain stem nuclei that project to the CNC.
the brain stem neurons which send their axons to the neurosecretory complex of the caudal brain.
the cytology of brain stem nuclei that contain neurons projecting to the CNC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HRP-labelled cells in the NMLF and DTMN are neurosecretory cells, whereas the cells in the RMN are non-neurosecretory neurons.
the neurons of the NMLF project to the CNC, and that these neurons are also connected to the midbrain DTMN.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HRP-labelled neurons in the RMN, NMLF and DTMN are all neurosecretory cells.
the brain stem projections to the CNC originate from the NMLF, the RMN and the neurons in the dorsal-lateral region of the medulla.
HRP-labelled profiles have been found in the NMLF, DTMN, RMN, and in neurons dorsal and lateral to the RMN.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HRP-labelled neurons in the RMN are not restricted to the RMN, but also extend into the dorsal-lateral area.

the neurons in the brain stem that project to the CNC are not restricted to the NMLL and RMN but are also found in other brain stem nuclei, and that the neurons in these other nuclei are not only HRP labelled but are also neurosecretory in nature.
